narrative: The model estimated an 85% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning that based on your application profile the bank considered repayment failure highly likely, so your loan was denied. The strongest factor was your checking-account status: it shows a negative balance, while most approved applicants have no negative balance. This pushed the decision toward bad credit. The second most influential factor was the amount requested: you asked for about 10,297 DM, far above the approved-applicant average of roughly 3,020 DM, which made the application look riskier. The third was the requested loan duration: 48 months is much longer than the approved average of about 19 months, increasing concern about sustained repayment. All three leading factors moved the prediction toward denial; other details such as your existing paid credit history were not enough to offset them. To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account into good standing and avoiding overdrafts, reducing the amount you request or shortening the repayment period, and considering a smaller loan or adding a guarantor or collateral. It would also help to review your credit information with the bank and ask what specific balance, amount, and term would make your application more acceptable before reapplying.
